symptom: In a long conversation, task cards are compressed below their content height and clipped.
direct_cause: A bounded flex-column scroll container permits its direct children to shrink; overflow-hidden cards discard their content.
class_root: The scroll flow must own the non-shrinking row invariant for every card.
internal_only_reason: The existing approved panel already owns scroll geometry; this fixes its flex sizing without adding a component or framework.
invariants: Flow rows retain their content height and overflow is handled by the conversation scrollbar.
generality_proof: A single direct-child shrink-0 rule applies to every row emitted by V4FlowRow.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own scroll containment and direct-child sizing.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: All card kinds share the direct-child rule. Real Electron geometry compares clientHeight and scrollHeight after task/queue messages.
Observed overflow-hidden task card under long flow; the parent rule retains its entire content height.
All user, assistant, tool and task row DOM elements are direct children of the corrected flow.

recurrence.reason: Any long conversation can exhaust the available height.
same_class_scan: Observed live task geometry 116px content versus 39px client height

prevention.invariant: Conversation rows never flex-shrink below content.
prevention.failure_mode: Long content scrolls in the flow.
prevention.strategy: Apply shrink-0 at the shared direct-child boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: Replace default flex shrink at the existing scroll owner.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency change is needed to bind Nomi workspace ownership.

residual_risks: Geometry proof covers the existing card shapes; future row renderers must preserve the same scroll ownership.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The layout owner knows available height and all direct row types.
